SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 17.—(AP)—Fires crackled fiercely on through dry timber, brush and grass from central California to west Central Oregon tonight, still uncomfortably close to picturesque mother lode towns and San Francisco bay resort areas despite control operations. Twenty truck loads of fighters entered Westville, in Placer County, California, to reinforce tired crews trying to curb a blaze that scorched two mountain settlements and licked at the fringes of two others. Town Threatened, An old blaze flared into new activity two miles north of Yachats, Ore., endangering auto camps and burning log-loading stations. A strong southwest wind drove the flames toward Waldport, several miles away and 200 men went to the fire lines. Northern California, virtually untouched by rain since last June, offered ideal fodder for the red demon. Three persons died yesterday in the two-score fires which

1936-03-04.text: London, March 3. (INS)--Declaring "We have really no alternative in the present state of the world," the British government today published its anxiously awaited Parliamentary "white paper" announcing a vast new defense program for costly navy, army and air force increases in equipment and man power. Two new battleships, a score of cruisers and an aircraft carrier, mechanization of the army, and expansion of the air force to 1,790 first line fighting machines are projected immediately. Industry was called upon to mobilize to production of war equipment. Although no total figure of the cost of the huge program was included in the white paper, estimates now say a five year plan will take two billion dollars. Winston Churchill, who has headed both the admiralty and war office, was prominently mentioned unofficially today as the likely choice for special minister of defense to coordinate all

LONDON, March 14—(Reuters)—The Reuters correspondent in Addis Ababa reported today that it had been learned semi-officially that Emperor Haile Selassie probably will agree to peace negotiations within the framework of the League of Nations. Such an agreement would be in reply to an invitation issued yesterday by the “Committee of 13” of the League of Nations council at Geneva.

New York—(INS)—Col. Charles A. Lindbergh, now visiting in England, has written a letter to United States Senator A. Harry Moore urging him to rally his political influence behind Col. H. Norman Schwarzkopf in the efforts of Gov. Harold Hoffman to oust Schwarzkopf as head of the New Jersey state police, the Evening Journal says today in a copyrighted dispatch from Trenton. The newspaper attributes its information to an official source close to Senator Moore, who was governor of New Jersey at the time of the Lindbergh baby kidnapping. The letter, containing Col. Lindbergh’s first mention of the crime which cost the life of his infant son since Bruno Richard Hauptmann’s trial at Flemington, will shortly be made public by Senator Moore, it is said, since the famous flyer has advised that this be done if it “will be beneficial.” Col. Lindbergh’s letter, it is said, contains no mention of Gove

Madrid, March 3.—(AP)—A newspaper dispatch from Paris today hinted strongly of a marriage between King Edward VIII of Great Britain and the Infanta Maria Christina, 25-year-old daughter of former King Alfonso XIII of Spain. London, March 3.—(AP)—It was authoritatively stated tonight that a marriage between King Edward and the former Infanta Maria Christina of Spain, hinted at by a Spanish newspaper, is 'impossible' under a British law whereby the king cannot wed a Catholic.

, By International News Service. LONDON, March 4.—Sometimes the press annoys the Lindberghs, but that did not keep them from renting a “haunted house” where, according to the Kentish county folk, William Caxton, one of the legendary inventors of printing, sets up a press every moonlit night. The house, known as “Long Barn,” is located at Weald, near Sevenoaks, Kent, and Colonel and Mrs. Charles A. Lindbergh and their son, Jon, are moving in shortly, it was understood today. Tradition says Caxton was born there, and he is said to set his press up in the room where he first saw the light. Four ancient half-timbered cottages and a barn, made into one house, compose the 18-room building. An old English rose garden surrounds it, with a swimming pool, tennis courts, and miles of fields stretching away beyond. Nearly every room has an open fireplace, and an assortment of furniture covering seve

BAN FRANCISCO, March 4—- (UP)—George Bernard Shaw, in a striped gray suit and a striped pink shirt with tan tie, sputtered bits of wisdom and satire all over the deck of the British cruise ship Arandora Star on his arrival in the United States today. San Francisco was a “one horse town” to him because it had only four daily newspapers. The Golden Gate bridge, rising magnificently over the entrance to the harbor, was “a beastly thing with two red poles.” He said he wouldn't be alive in 1940 to visit the world's fair commemorating the opening of the bridge “unless someone offers to make an exhibition of me.” Shaw is going to the Grand Canyon, although he wanted to know what it is. “Is it a building?” he asked ship reporters who welcomed him for his second visit to the city.

Italy, victorious thus far in its military campaign against Ethiopia but facing increased sanctions by members of the League of Nations, abolished private banking today. The abolition was accomplished by the Italian cabinet, whose leader and majority member, Premier Mussolini, declared a renewed defiance of sanctions. Thus far, the only sanctions declared against Italy have been financial and economic — leading to the sweeping banking reform in Italy. However, the diplomats assembled at Geneva talked of applying the more stringent punishment of an embargo against oil shipments to the nation which is fighting Ethiopia. A report was published in London that Emperor Haile Selassie had sued for peace at Geneva, but the activities of the League of Nations would not serve to substantiate this angle.

TOKYO — (®) — The aristocratic Prince Konoye declined today an opportunity to become Japan's youngest premier, sending Emperor Hirohito and his advisers on a new search for a man who will be able to head the government in its crisis. A communique from the martial law headquarters disclosed that more than 1,400 officers and men participated in the rebellion which broke out at dawn last Wednesday.

1936-04-03.text: Reports reaching Rome today said strategic Lake Tana, center of British interests in Ethiopia, had been reached by Italians. In London, informed sources envisaged peace negotiations between Italy and Ethiopia after the sudden departure from Addis Ababa of the emperor's advisor. In the meantime, Germany informed Britain that it refused to promise not to fortify the Rhineland.

LONDON, April 3, ()- A point-blank German refusal to promise not to fortify the Rhineland, even temporarily, was delivered to the British government today. It arrived at the foreign office shortly before Anthony Eden, foreign secretary, went to the House of Commons to announce that Great Britain, France and Belgium were ready to fight as allies if attacked by Germany but that the British government was anxious to discuss permanent peace proposals with Reichsfuehrer Hitler. It was understood that the final answer was delivered to Eden by Joachim Von Ribbentrop, Hitler's special ambassador, in a five-minute talk before Eden went to the House of Commons to outline the conditions under which Anglo-French-Belgian general staffs will confer in London. Paris, April 2.—()—France massed her diplomatic resources today for a counter-attack against Germany’s Locarno plan. Foreign Minister Pierre-Etienne Flandin summoned the French ambassadors in London, Berlin, Brussels and Rome to come to Paris for a two-fold campaign, Map Course of Action First, informed sources said, the government resolved to present a strong attitude against Germany's violation of the Locarno pact by remilitarization of the Rhineland until after France's parliamentary elections April 26 and May 3. Second, these sources said, the government would employ tactics of delay while searching for a peace plan more favorable to France. Rightists Take Lead The stern opposition to Germany’s treaty breach came, informed sources said, while rightist leaders were utilizing the government’s failure to punish Germany as evidence that Hitler had outmaneuvered France. - Gravesend, Kent, Eng. —(?)— Mrs. Amy Johnson Mollison started off from here today on what was believed to be an attempt to set a new flight record to Cape Town, South Africa. The British flier took off at 5:30 a.m. in a pale blue and gray monoplane. It carried 127 gallons of gasoline, sufficient for 2,200 miles non-stop.

(International News Service) - LONDON, April 2.—Coronation of King Edward VIII will take place in May, 1937, Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin announced today in the House of Commons. The exact date will be announced later.

| LONDON, April 3 (4)—Shocked and angered by the receipts of what it considers irrefutable proof that the Italians are using poison gas in Ethiopia, the British government indicated tonight that it is preparing to strike at Premier Mussolini with pressure for an oil embargo against Italy unless he agrees to a quick cessation of hostilities. An authoritative source declared that the British will ask Salvador De Madariaga of Spain, president of the League of Nations’ sanctions committee—the “committee of 13”—to call that body into session immediately to determine the prospects for peace in order to clear the way for further sanctions against Italy if Mussolini is not ready to call an armistice. It was stated that the British want the session early next week.

Paris, April 2 ()—France will reply to Adolf Hitler’s peace plan by asserting its acceptance would mean the death of the League of Nations, officials said tonight. The government also probably will ask for a hurried conference with Great Britain, Belgium and Italy, at which it will demand rejection of the German counter-proposals. Officials said a response to Hitler’s offer drafted by Premier Albert Sarraut and Foreign Minister Pierre-Etienne Flandin tomorrow will denounce der Reichsführer’s declaration but will say France is not closing the door to negotiations. The reply, which will take the form of a speech or statement since Germany did not address the plan to France, will hold the proposals unacceptable because Hitler offered no concessions to enable France to respect international law. “Germany must be made to realize that her violation of Locarno, hard on the heels of so many conc

Berlin, April 2-1) Adolf Hitler’s long-awaited program to insure peace in western Europe, envisaging 25-year peace pacts with France and Belgium and Germany's return to the League of Nations, was delivered yesterday to the British government. This lengthy document, one of the most important pronouncements on foreign policy by der Führer in his three years of rule, was hailed in official quarters here as a constructive and far-reaching move. The general view was that Hitler’s program, outlined in counter-proposals delivered to Great Britain following his rejection of the plan drawn by the four Locarno powers, goes much further than Hitler's original proposals, advanced March 7 when he denounced the Locarno treaty. Among the chief features of Hitler’s program are: Negotiations for a “new Locarno” would be carried on for a period of four months, Germany, France, and Belgium would consent to

1936-01-23.text: London, Jan. 23. (4?)—The body of King George V was returned to London this afternoon for four days lying in state in the capital of his former empire. The new king, Edward VIII, who accompanied the body of his father, already had communicated to the House of Commons the declaration, “I am resolved to follow in the way he has set before me.” London, Jan. 23 (UP)—King George's sorrowing family turned the body over today to the people he loved and served. It will lie in state until Tuesday. It was brought to London in a coach funeral train after a brief funeral service. The body on a gun carriage was borne along two and one half miles of winding country road heavy with frost to the station. King Edward VIII and other males of the family walking behind it. Queen Mary and the women in carriages. Queen Mary cried as she watched the body of her husband put into a black painted funeral coach. A

Copyright 1936 by The Associated Press LONDON, Jan. 23.—(#)—King George V came home in death today for last sad rites in the capital of his empire, followed sorrowfully afoot by his first born son, now Edward VIII, the new monarch of Great Britain and her dominions. This morning his body lay in the tiny vine-enshrouded church of his Sandringham estate, where he died. This afternoon, brought over the 100 miles to London, it lay in state under the 500-year-old arched wooden ceiling of Westminster Hall, where George’s subjects, until late Monday night, will be permitted to pass in silence to pay their last respects. On a warm, sunny day last May King George, smiling and buoyantly happy at the outpouring of love and devotion of his subjects in celebration of his silver jubilee, drove with his queen through the same streets over which he was carried today—in death. (Copyright, 1956, by The Associated Press) Sandringham, Eng., Jan. 21 (Tuesday)—Great Britain’s beloved King George died peacefully last night just before midnight. The Prince of Wales, his 41-year-old bachelor son, automatically became King of the world’s largest empire. The kindly, 70-year-old George V was unconscious at the end. Queen Mary, the Prince of Wales and other members of the royal family and the Archbishop of Canterbury were at the bedside when he died at 11:55 P. M. (6:55 P. M. Eastern Standard Time). A sudden, four-day illness caused His Majesty’s death. He suffered an attack of bronchial catarrh, accompanied by heart weakness. Weeping, the Queen was led away supported by her eldest son—the new King—and the chamber was darkened. Later today the monarch’s body will be taken to Sandringham church and then removed to London to lie in state in Westminster Abbey for final tribu

LONDON, Jan. 20 (#)—Rudyard Kipling is going to rest in the poet's corner at Westminster Abbey. The noted author, who died Saturday morning, five days after he underwent an emergency operation for a perforated stomach ulcer, will be buried Thursday in that last resting place of Britain's famous sons. The Very Rev. William Foxley Norris, dean of Westminster, announced the funeral service would be held at noon.

London, Jan. 22. ()—Edward VIII was proclaimed king today and began the 39th rule of the British people since the Norman conquest. From his throne, the 41-year-old bachelor, with a new solemnity, plunged into the affairs of state. He conferred with Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin and then sadly returned to Sandringham. There his dead father, George V, attended by country folk, rests in the Parish church. Tomorrow his body will be brought to London by special train. It will lie in state in Westminster Hall until Monday night. Burial with a great state funeral ceremonial will take place Tuesday at Windsor. From the balcony of St. James’ Palace, at Charing Cross, again at Temple Bar, and finally at the Royal Exchange, the new king was publicly proclaimed. Ten thousand troops lined the streets while picturesque trumpeters sounded a fanfare and a 41-gun salute boomed in the honor of the man wh

Associated Press Staff Writer. Premier Mussolini carried his diplomatic war controversy deeper into the League of Nations council today by striking out against the five-power mutual aid agreement and British naval maneuvers in the Mediterranean. One of his spokesmen asserted he would protest the assistance pact of Great Britain, France, Turkey, Greece and Yugoslavia as an "anti-Italian alliance." He was further reported ready to criticize the concentration of British warships near the scene of fighting in the Italo-Ethiopian war. EMBARGO CONSIDERED While these diplomatic campaigns took definite form, a new committee was called to consider the proposed coal, steel, and iron embargo against the aggressor nation in the East African conflict. Its deliberations concerned principally the potential effectiveness of such measures.

London—Rudyard Kipling was buried today alongside other immortals of English literature. While the body of his sovereign, the late King George V, was being borne to Westminster Hall, the ashes of Kipling were placed reverently in the dim and quiet poet’s corner of Westminster Abbey. In the shallow depth of earth below the tiling, scored with inscriptions to many a great name, the bard’s dust will mingle with that of Chaucer, Spenser, Samuel Johnson, Macaulay, Tennyson and Browning. Kipling died in a London hospital last Friday night, three days before King George passed away at Sandringham.

LONDON (W2BP) — The body of King George V was borne between lanes of hundreds of thousands of his sorrowing countrymen through the streets of London and was laid in state in Westminster Hall Thursday for the highest and lowest of his subjects to pay homage. The royal family relinquished the king's body to the temple for the next five days until the burial at Windsor on Tuesday among his ancestors. King George V will lie in the great hall for the people to file by for one last look at his face. The body brought by royal funeral train from Sandringham was carried through the streets on a gun carriage draped in royal mourning with the priceless crown of Britain resting on the royal standard above it. The crowd, all in mourning, stood with bowed heads. The sobbing of women could be heard falling along the line. Otherwise, the great city of London was in hushed silence. Behind the coffin walk

1936-04-15.text: London, Apr. 14.—A direct Anglo-French clash over sanctions against Italy at Geneva Friday, if peace talks are not productive, appeared probable tonight. In authoritative quarters it was said the British cabinet instructed Foreign Secretary Eden to take the strongest stand against the League's “abandonment” of Ethiopia should peace negotiations fail. Eden is expected to take a position in further defense of Ethiopia rather than agree to an expected French move for lifting the sanctions. A conference between Eden and Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin indicated tonight it was said authoritatively, that the government is prepared to support and may even demand further economic and financial sanctions against Italy. Military sanctions probably will be held in abeyance because it is known France is opposed to them. The British are not yet convinced

By The Associated Press The conference of the British and Belgian army general staffs was begun today in London, simultaneously with the start of negotiations for settlement of the Italo-Ethiopian war, to decide on measures to insure against any unprovoked aggression. Although the conversations between the general staffs were to be conducted in secret, the British government constantly had assured the public no new political affiliations would arise from their decisions. Pay Tribute to Ambassador While the military leaders assembled for their discussions, final tribute was being paid by the British empire to the late ambassador from Germany, Leopold von Hoesch, whose body was taken aboard a British warship bound for his homeland. The peace talks of the League of Nations at Geneva presented a greater uncertainty as to the future course of European peace than did the problem of settlement

PARIS, April 14.—(4)—A proposal for a “United States of Arabia” is being promoted by Great Britain in an effort to align Arabs against further Italian expansion in the Red Sea region, nationalist sources said today. It is believed the dream of an Arabian empire, consisting of most of the kingdoms, mandated territories and protectorates forming the Arabian peninsula, is moving rapidly toward fulfillment. Recent demonstrations, pointing to great Arabian unity, are seen as a sign favorable to ultimate fruition of the plan.

LONDON, Apr. 15. (UP)--More than 60 miners were killed today when the winding gear of an elevator broke at the Sumitomo coal mine in Fukuoka prefecture of Japan, the Exchange Telegraph Tokyo correspondent reported. Shifts were being changed at daybreak, the correspondent said, when broken cables sent 83 men plunging 2,000 feet to the bottom of the shaft. About 20 were found alive, the correspondent said, all desperately injured and likely to die.

France and Great Britain, who have stood shoulder to shoulder in most of Europe’s 20th century crisis, appeared headed Tuesday toward a serious disagreement. Conflicting views toward Premier Mussolini’s ‘colonial adventure’ was the shoal on which the now traditional allies might run aground. The League of Nations is seeking peace terms from Ethiopia and Italy. The British fear Il Duce will not cooperate in the Geneva attempt to end the war unless given his way in Ethiopia. In that event, the British want additional sanctions placed on Italy. France, eager for the backing of Mussolini's million-man army in the Rhineland crisis, wants the present financial and economic barriers against Italy lowered. The beginning of the tri-power general staff conferences, arising from Germany's remilitarization of the Rhineland, coincided with preliminary Italo-Ethiopian negotiations at Geneva, under the auspices of the League of Nations, for East African peace. The British, French and Belgian officers decided to undertake immediately their consultations on practical measures to ensure security against any unprovoked aggression despite the absence of Italy, the fourth remaining Locarno power, from the conference table. LONDON, April 14, (P)—Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin has called into urgent consultation Lord Tyrell of Avon, the ‘one-man brain trust’ of British diplomacy, to help salve one of the gravest dilemmas in British foreign policy since the World War, it was understood today. The veteran diplomatist was called to the prime minister’s country retreat, it was understood, to advise him on a new double crisis: the Italo-Ethiopian and Franco-German disputes. It was believed he advised Baldwin to concentrate efforts on ‘retaining possibilities of effecting peace negotiations between Italy and Ethiopia, accompanied by an armistice of any armed action which might prejudice peace.

LOS ANGELES.— (#) —Freddie Bartholomew, child film star, was “not at home” Tuesday to representatives of his mother, Mrs. Lillian Mae Bartholomew. Leonard J. Meyberg, lawyer for Mrs. Bartholomew, who arrived here Monday from New York after a trip from England, said that he had sent representatives to young Bartholomew's Beverly Hills house and they had been turned away by servants.

1936-11-27.text: LONDON, Nov. 27--(P)—Scores of threatening letters addressed to Wallis Warfield Simpson have caused elaborate precautions to be taken to protect King Edward’s American friend. In addition to the patrolmen always on duty before her lavish Cumberland Terrace home, it was learned today from a reliable source another police officer has been assigned to special duty guarding her against infernal machines. While friends were discussing this latest disclosure of the private life of Mrs. Simpson, her former husband, Ernest A. Simpson, whom she divorced, met Mrs. Jacques A. L. Raffray of New York when she debarked from a liner at Southampton, and accompanied her to London in the same compartment. In efforts to escape public attention, they darted off the boat train in London and ran separately from the station. They dived into the same car, however, and lay on the floorboards. London, — (AP) — The British cabinet met in a sudden “emergency” session today and, informed sources said, discussed the question of belligerent rights for both sides in the Spanish civil war. It was understood the ministers, meeting for one hour, reviewed the entire Spanish situation. They were called together after the admiralty had announced that the Spanish insurgent dictator-designate, Gen. Francisco Franco, had acceded to repeated British demands by establishing safety zones for neutral shipping at Barcelona, which he has threatened to bombard. At the same time, the subcommittee on international nonintervention in Spain met at the foreign office and decided to refer to the full committee a plan for sending neutral observers to the Spanish borders to guard against foreign arms importations.

By the Associated Press The Spanish Insurgent General Francisco Franco Thursday night surrendered to British demands he provide safety zones for neutral vessels in Barcelona harbor should he try to blow the town up as he threatened. With the international tension of the civil war thus somewhat eased, 76 Americans ate a strange Thanksgiving dinner on the road from Madrid to Valencia to which they were being evacuated by the U.S. Department of State which closed the Madrid embassy. Americans at Barcelona also were advised to leave. There were 22 other Americans, mostly newspapermen and businessmen, who stayed in the embassy in Madrid within sound of the battle for possession of the University City area. Fascists fought forward slowly in efforts to reach the sides of their 2,000 comrades marooned by government lines around the clinic hospital building which an international column of anti-f

LONDON, Nov. 27—(?)}—A marked cooling off of the British attitude toward Germany and Italy was reported in informed circles today as the cabinet met in “emergency” session for what was understood to be a review of the entire Spanish situation. These sources said that Great Britain had rejected an “overture” to join the recently signed German-Japanese anti-Communism pact. Poland, which recently reached an agreement with Great Britain that neither would join pacts dividing Fascist and Leftist powers into opposing groups, was said to have rejected a similar proposal. Britain was represented as watching and waiting to see whether Fascist powers will extend to General Francisco Franco the aid deemed necessary even for the capture of Madrid.

Francisco Franco, Nationalist dictator, had designated a neutral zone for foreign ships as Great Britain demanded. But fresh trouble was expected before the day was over. Tour Discussed The King-Simpson subject shared the cabinet’s attention with a discussion of Edward's recent tour of depression areas in Wales, according to the rumors. Opposition within the cabinet to the king's apparent desire to marry Mrs. Simpson reportedly has been complicated by further misunderstanding with the king. DUBLIN, Irish Free State, Nov. 27 (AP)—The Irish Parliament defeated an opposition motion seeking recognition of the Spanish insurgents as the government of Spain today, 65 to 44.

London, Nov. 27.—The British Admiralty said yesterday that the Spanish insurgent general, Francisco Franco, had granted Great Britain’s repeated demands for neutral shipping safety zones in Barcelona harbor. 1936-10-14.text: Moscow, Oct. 14 (4) - Soviet Russia demanded establishment of a virtual blockade of Portugal by the British and French navies to halt supplies of arms for Spanish insurgents, officials disclosed tonight. The demand was made by Russian diplomatic officials to Lord Plymouth, chairman of the international non-intervention committee, in London today. Immediate establishment of "control" over Portuguese ports, it stated, is the only way to end the supply of arms to the Fascist armies in Spain. An official communique stated: "We demand from the committee the establishment of such control. We suggest the enforcement of the control measures be turned over to the French or British fleet or both."

LONDON, Oct. 14 (®—Soviet Russia's ambassador, in a personal plea to the British foreign office, demanded today, informed sources said, that the international neutrality committee be summoned this week to act on Moscow's charges of flagrant Fascist violation of the “hands off Spain” accord. Ivan M. Maisky, the ambassador, who returned from Moscow only last night, lost no time in personally assuming charge of Russia's case against Italy, Germany and Portugal, which it has accused of sending military aid to Spain's insurgents. He descended on the foreign office while the British cabinet assembled across the street and called on Lord Plymouth, British chairman of the non-intervention committee. It was understood Ambassador Maisky flatly informed Lord Plymouth that Russia considered a week ample time for the Fascist states to reply to the Soviet charges, detailed at last Friday’s committee s

London, Oct. 14. (FP) — Ernest Simpson and Mrs. Wallis Simpson, King Edward’s American friend, moved today - he to his club, she to a new apartment. An informed source said Simpson’s personal effects were moved from Bryanston Court apartments and that the London commercial broker had taken up residence at his famed military club, by virtue of his former membership in the Coldstream Guards. Mrs. Simpson, alone, moved to her new home in Cumberland Terrace, facing Regents Park, a mile from Buckingham Palace. Since she returned last month as a member of the party which accompanied the king on his Dalmatian Coast holiday, Mrs. Simpson has not lived at Bryanston Court.

MES. SIMPSON DIVORCE? CHICAGO, Oct 14 (UP) The Chicago Daily News said today that W. Simpson, believed to be Mrs. Wallace Simpson, friend of King Edward VIII of England, had filed suit in London for a divorce from E. Simpson.

WASHINGTON, Oct. 13.—(/)— Formation of a “gold bloc” by America, France and Britain, with almost a monopoly of the world gold supply, was described in financial quarters today as a powerful inducement toward monetary stabilization by other nations. Treasury officials shied off from suggestions that the tri-power control of gold might be used to force other nations into line, but said they expected other governments to join the “gold bloc.” A movement by other governments to join the monetary pact was forecast as a “natural development” by responsible administration officials. Under terms of the agreement, effective today, the three dominant financial powers pledged themselves to sell gold only to each other or to any nation which subsequently may become a party to the accord.
By Associated Press NEW YORK, Oct. 14.—Major James Mollison, British flier, plans to start next week on a west-to-east crossing of the Atlantic from New York to England.

London—(/P)—King Edward scrapped another royal precedent Wednesday—the annual Christmas broadcast to the empire. The British monarch made known through his secretary he does not intend to follow his father’s custom.

TOKYO, (%. The Japanese government was aroused by reports of a British loan to China, fearful that such a loan might be intended for currency reform or replenishment of Chinese armaments. Japanese officials, pushing their own program of economic development in Manchoukuo and penetration into North China, explained that Tokyo does not object to a constructive loan to China to further rehabilitation of the country. But, they added, the Japanese government will oppose vigorously any loan that might have political implications, or be intended for currency reform or replenishment of armaments. Reports of the loan, advanced by informed observers here, were coupled also with the rumors of an aerial development agreement between Britain and China.
