London—(#)—Proud heralds in the trappings of another age proclaimed a new king today—and from the warship Fury’s decks the man who was a monarch watched another, foreign shore. Throngs, rapt and prideful, spread out before the musty battlements of St. James’ while trumpets shrilled and Sir Gerald Wollaston, the Garter principal king of arms, proclaimed George VI “the only lawful liege lord of 495,000,000 people. At Boulogne-Sur-Mer, France, flustered officialdom, mobile guards, detectives and police waited for the destroyer Fury, bearing Edward of England, to anchor off the port. A train, with one whole car reserved, may carry the king of only yesterday toward Zurich, Switzerland—thence to Italy, to Austria, to a Swiss Alpine resort, to the Dalmatian coast or wherever he will wait, in lonely vigil, for Wallis Warfield Simpson. Hundreds of curious swarmed the channel waterfront, expecting

London. —- (AP) —- His Royal Highness the Duke of Windsor is the new title King George has picked for his brother, the former King Edward, it was reported reliably today. An official announcement was expected to be made later today.

London, (4%--They cried in Hongkong While the sun climbed up at Singapore, they listened and raised a sobbing cheer. They swallowed hard, with lumps in their throats, in Saskatchewan. They heard him through the black and icy night of Hudson Bay, and cried real tears. Wherever there is a “little bit of England,” and wherever dwell England’s friends and cousins too, the hearts of men and women beat hard last night and today to the voice from Windsor. “At last,” said Prince Edward Windsor, “I am able to say a few words of my OWN ..< Power Is Felt Wherever they heard it, in a steaming kitchen in Wyoming or salon on the Champs Elysees, they felt its power. And they cried, from the Shetlands to the Antipodes, “bravely done!” It was as a man, yet a man introduced as “His Highness, Prince Edward,” that the passing sovereign of all that is Britain's spoke from the Augusta Tower of Windsor Castle

Dublin, Irish Free State, Dec. 11. —(AP)—In the only land where tonight Edward VIII still is king, the Free State parliament pushed to final passage a bill abolishing the office of governor-general, king's representative. Thus, the Free State made itself in effect independent of Britain in the conduct of internal affairs, although President Eamon de Valera made clear that there would be no break from the empire. To Ratify Accession De Valera planned to present to the dail tomorrow legislation ratifying the accession of King George VI, but without that legislation tonight Edward still was technically king.

1936-07-02.text: (Associated Press Foreign Staff) GENEVA, July 1—#—Anthony Eden of Great Britain told the League of Nations Assembly today it should not, in any way, recognize Italy's conquest of Ethiopia. He declared, however, that sanctions had failed and that “only military action could succeed” in changing the situation. “In present world conditions this could not be considered as a possibility,” the British Foreign Secretary added. He recommended the continuance, after the Assembly has taken action to suppress sanctions, of mutual assistance pacts in the Mediterranean Sea. Eden spoke while Geneva heard warnings of wholesale resignations of smaller powers from the League, and after the Assembly had listened to biting criticism of great powers from the South African delegate because of their recession from sanctions. The South African delegate, Charles T. Water, recalled the noble protestations “of Br

GENEVA, July 1—(AP)—Three of the world’s greatest powers rallied in support of a Fascist-shelled League of Nations structure tonight in the face of veiled hints of withdrawals by smaller nations. The three were Great Britain, France and Soviet Russia. Spokesmen for the first two said their governments would not recognize Italy's annexation of Ethiopia and all voiced continued faith in the league's future. Journalists Expelled These expressions of hope came with notes of bitter disillusionment as the statesmen surveyed the wreckage of their effort to save Ethiopia from what they branded as aggression. Eight Italian newspapermen, arrested for “creating a scandal” by heckling and cursing Emperor Haile Selassie when he addressed the assembly yesterday, were released from jail and immediately expelled from Switzerland. (Italy, standing behind the newspapermen, ordered its minister to Switzerl

WIMBLEDON, ENG. (#)— Helen Jacobs of Berkeley, Calif, four times American champion, gained the final round of the All-England tennis championship today with a 6-4, 6-2 victory over Jadwiga Jedrzejowska of Poland. Miss Jacobs’ opponent in the final to be played Saturday will be Frau Hilda Krahwinkel Sperling of Germany and Denmark. Frau Sperling conquered Mme. Simone Mathieu of France, 6-3, 6-2. Miss Jacobs’ victory today atoned for two previous defeats at the hands of the plump Polish star and marked the third straight year and the fifth time since 1929 that she has reached the final. Frau Sperling was an unsuccessful finalist five years ago.

STINNETT, July 1 (4)~Monte Bridges was convicted today of murder in the Feb. 1, slaying of Fred English, Borger Hotel proprietor, and sentenced to 25 years in prison. The jury brought in its verdict after deliberating 16 hours. Defense counsel in its arguments to the jury pleaded self-defense on the grounds English had threatened to kill the defendant. The state's attorneys said English could not have been making a move toward Bridges at the time of the shooting for the wound was in the hotel proprietor’s side.

Washington, — Following Japan's refusal to sign the London armament treaty limiting battleship naval operations, Admiral William Standley, chief of naval operations, indicated yesterday that the two new capital vessels to be built next year by this country will carry 16-inch armament.

NICE, France, July 12—Alexander Berkman, the internationally-known anarchist, died June 28 in a hospital here of a self-inflicted bullet wound, it was disclosed today. The oft-jailed friend of Emma Goldman, with whom he was deported from the United States in 1920, was 66 years old. Hospital authorities said Berkman was taken to the hospital with a bullet in his chest. He had been found, wounded, in his home in Nice.

GENEVA, June 30 (UP)—Riotous scenes of cursing and fighting in the galleries shattered the dignity of the League of Nations assembly tonight when black-robed little Emperor Haile Selassie told the world leaders, "you deserted us to Italy." Police were called in to restore order after a chorus of heckling, boos, and curses greeted the emperor without an empire when he rose to make a final appeal for aid. Persons alleged to be supporters of the negus started the tumult shouting curses at the emperor. Fighting broke out as the emperor said what he had to say, calmly and with fury. At midnight, it was announced that eight newspapermen who were dragged from the assembly were placed formally under investigation and charged with "creating scandal in the League of Nations," on the basis of their actions. Police said those arrested would spend the night in jail and be brought before the federal p

ROME, July 1—(AP)—The Ital- ian government today ordered a protest to Switzerland against the arrest at Geneva yesterday of eight Italian newspapermen who hissed Emperor Haile Selassie of Ethiopia in the League of Nations’ assembly. The Italian minister in Berne was instructed to deliver the protest personally. All Fascist organizations in Rome gathered late today for a demonstration against the Swiss action. The newspapermen, who threw the assembly into an uproar, were sent a multitude of congratulatory messages from all over Italy. Umberto Guglielmotti, secretary of the Italian journalists syndicate, telegraphed them he was proud of their gesture. On the other hand, a number of telegrams arrived from Geneva which Italian authorities said “insulted” Italian journalists.

1936-12-17.text: LONDON. (UP). Five British cruisers scheduled to be scrapped under the Anglo-American naval treaty will be retained in service because "this is no time to scrap serviceable vessels." Sir Samuel Hoare, first lord of the admiralty, informed the house of commons. Reliable sources disclosed that Britain has developed a new 14-inch gun more efficient than the 16-inch guns of other navies, and will use it in two 35,000-ton battleships to be started next month. BARCELONA. (UP). Spurred by the first rebel bombardment of the Catalonian coast, the government of Luis Companys, president of the semi-autonomous state, reached a speedy solution of a political crisis. Announcement of a new cabinet was made, breaking the deadlock precipitated three days ago when Prime Minister Jose Tarradellas and his cabinet resigned because they "could not control the extremists." HENDAYE, France, — Uncensored reports

LONDON (7?) — Great Britain was disclosed today to have laid down five times as much naval tonnage in 1936 as she did three years ago. Sir Samuel Hoare, first lord of the admiralty, who made the announcement in a speech last night, earlier told the House of Commons he would ask bids for new capital ships to be laid down soon. The new battleships will be the King George V and the Prince of Wales. They already have been authorized but their keels may not be laid until after Jan. 1, under the terms of the 1930 London naval agreement.

Manchester, Ia., Dec. 17.—(4—Authorities announced here today that John H. Scherbring, 48-year-old Colesburg farmer, has confessed to writing two extortion letters to Miss Vinnie Lovett, 57, reputedly wealthy Colesburg woman, after he had been captured last night. He is being held in the Delaware county jail here on a federal charge of using the mails to extort. The letters, it was said, were written in longhand with an indelible pencil and were signed "The Black Legion." Each letter, authorities said, demanded $3,500, the second of which said that unless the demands were met, that the woman "would be kidnapped and would not see Colesburg again." Authorities charged Scherbring said he wrote the notes because he has an $8,000 mortgage on his 80-acre farm, he has a wife and four children to support, and he has other debts amounting to $4,000 which have been pressing him. London, Dec. 17 (INS)—While an influenza epidemic spread through the royal family today, the Duke of Windsor was reported to have sent a message to his brother and successor pleading with the new king to silence the archbishop of Canterbury and other persistent critics of the ex-ruler. Baron Brownlow, close friend of both Mrs. Wallis Simpson and former King Edward, is on his way from the ex-King’s retreat, Castle Enzesfeld, Austria, to London, according to the Daily Express. Besides turning his back on the Church of England by planning a civil wedding, the Duke of Windsor hoped later to reply to the archbishop but feels that he cannot now in his present position. Because of that fact, however, he is said to have asked King George to use the influence of the crown to prevent any further unanswerable criticism. The House of Commons met today in crackling tension, with leaders buzzing about

By The Associated Press Enzesfeld, Austria — Edward, Duke of Windsor, was represented today as ready if not eager to drop his role of a semi-recluse and come forward soon with a few words and pictures for the newspapers. Further information believed to be reliable said the former king of England was considering a proposal to go deer hunting in Styria. In contrast to his earlier apparent moroseness, Edward sat up late last night listening to a broadcast. The Baroness Rothschild, it was learned, last evening won Edward over to her suggestion that he make a Christmas shopping tour in Vienna and perhaps even visit some of the night clubs.

HENDAYE, France, Dec. 17.—Uncensored reports from war-torn Madrid quoted reliable sources today as having said the Madrid government is convinced that only with definite foreign aid can it defeat the Spanish Fascists. Recognition of Gen. Francisco Franco's Insurgent regime by Italy and Germany struck a death blow at the Madrid cause, its leaders felt, just at a time when the city’s unexpected defenses seemed to be turning the tide of battle in its favor. Most of the informed leaders in Madrid, the uncensored reports said, feel that Russia, acting alone, cannot carry the role of Madrid's savior any longer. Disappointed in France The wariness of France in not becoming involved is one of the major disappointments to the workers class which, from the beginning of the war, believed it could depend upon the French proletariat for aid. By The Associated Press Nanking said the rebel Marshal Chang Hsuei-Liang would be given a “final chance” to free his prisoner, Generalissimo Chiang Kai-Shek. If he refused, it was declared, the government's full striking force would be thrown against him. A punitive expedition against the rebels was ordered. The government claimed the rebel stronghold, Sianfu, already was surrounded, Nanking spokesmen persisted in assertions that the generalissimo was alive and unharmed at Sianfu. An American aviator, Royal Leonard, was reported “detained” at Sianfu, presumably by Marshal Chang's troops.

1936-03-05.text: | LONDON, Mar, 4. — (W.P)—Col. Charles A. Lindbergh has leased the rambling Kentish country house in which Caxton, England’s first printer, is reputed to have been born and where his ghost is supposed to linger. The house is known as “Long Barn.

Glasgow, Scotland, Mar. 5. (P)— King Edward was cheered as “good old Teddy” by 2,000 workmen on the new liner, Queen Mary, today. The Scottish nickname for Edward was shouted as he completed a two-and-three-quarter hours inspection tour of the partially completed ship. The king remarked, “This is a ship built for utility,” and expressed his desire to visit it again before the maiden voyage in May. His majesty was informed that the service speed of the liner will be 29 knots. Thousands of persons thronged the streets to see Edward on his first visit to Scotland as king.

LONDON, March 4 (4)—The Little Count Haugwitz-Reventlow, already known as the world’s richest baby, may also be the world’s most costly baby, an authoritative source said today. His mother, the former Barbara Hutton who is now pronounced well on the road to recovery after complications followed the birth of her first child, is likely to pay about $6,000 in doctor’s fees for him, this source said—but will have an opportunity to contribute $600,000 more to hospital charities as a thanks offering. British specialists such as Lord Horder, physician in ordinary to King Edward, and the five other specialists in the countess’ case, do not discuss actual fees. These are arranged by the family doctor who called in the specialists, one of whom said, “they are probably a good deal less than they would be in America.” Should Barbara desire to show her gratitude for the physicians by charitable donat

HOLLYWOOD, Calif. (P)—Glamorous Marlene Dietrich, Teutonic screen star, is headed for the London films, leaving Paramount studios with a picture but at the moment—no star. The blonde actress walked off the set of “I Loved A Soldier” nearly a fortnight ago, at the same time Ernest Lubitsch lost his job as Paramount’s production chief after a tiff with Mae West. Her business agent, Harry Edington, said she will cross the Atlantic within a month or six weeks to join the constantly growing list of American screen stars playing in London productions.

London, March 4 ()—A middle-aged German lawyer-writer, accused of espionage upon Great Britain's air force, heard documents read in Old Bailey Court today tending to implicate him in spying against American air forces during the World War. The trial, Great Britain's first one for espionage since the war, saw the defendant, Dr. Hermann Gortz, blink when he heard his own description of himself as a “dangerous intelligence officer” turned against him. The crown presented a document Gortz had written to the German government describing his intelligence work during the World War and mentioning he lived for a year and a half in the United States and three and a half years in London. During that period, the letter said, he was “again in contact with American and English war-time aviators” and “I am even now still in touch with military aviators on the active list, or I probably can get in touch

(By Associated Press) LONDON, March 4—A letter in which Dr. Hermann Gortz, German lawyer and writer, said he had been able to extract information from American and English aviators was read by the prosecutor today at the opening of his trial for espionage. Dr. Gortz, speaking excellent English, pleaded not guilty to charges of violating the British Official Secrets Act at the start of his hearing in Old Bailey court—England’s first foreign spy trial since the end of the world war. Two women were among those selected for the jury. The prosecutor read a letter dated Hamburg, Sept. 15, 1935, on a sheet of paper headed, “Dr. Hermann Gortz, solicitor and specialist on English law, the United States of American law.” The letter said: “I point out that I consider myself particularly suitable for employment in the intelligence service” within what the applicant called the “sphere of the German a

LONDON.—(?) — The staggering cost of empire defense began to dawn Wednesday night on a public still digesting details of the greatest peace time armament program ever launched in Great Britain. Members of parliament learned that the regular defense requirements for the next fiscal year, irrespective of the special program disclosed in a white paper Tuesday, total 155,250,000 pounds (about $775,000,000) which is 31,000,000 pounds more than in 1935.

ASMARA, Eritrea, March 4 (4)— An unofficial report said the bodies of three unidentified white men had been found today in the recent battle area between the Tembien sector and Amba Alaji. Fascists guessed the three, as yet unidentified, may have been a British doctor, an Indian doctor and an Austrian, whose addresses were found on two Poles captured recently and sent to Italy. These doctors were with an Ethiopian Red Cross unit. The Italian high command estimated today that 30,000 Ethiopians were killed or wounded in fighting since the big Italian drives started February 10. Italian slain was estimated at 9,000.

1936-07-29.text: | DETROIT, July 2—im—K. T. Keller, president of the Chrysler corporation, announced today an additional cash bonus of $2,000,000 will be distributed August 10 to employees in the United States, Canada, England and Belgium. The bonus will be the second paid by the corporation this year, $2,300,000 having been distributed to employees on February 14. During the past six months the corporation has produced 578,407 automobiles and trucks, the largest six months business in its history, Keller said.

Miami, Fla., July 25 (4°)—-A tropical storm moved across Florida’s extreme southern tip tonight, leaving the east coast resort belt unscathed. A utility lineman was burned fatally at Miami during preparations for the storm that crossed the Gulf Stream from the British Bahamas, but up to 9 P. M., the highest wind here was the 37 miles an hour recorded at 8:30 P. M. The disturbance, bringing winds of near hurricane force to isolated lighthouses off the coast and sparsely settled Key Largo, 40 miles south, was said by the weather bureau to be moving west northwestward across the flat lands of Florida's tip, some 60 miles south of Miami. Meteorologist George K.E. Dunn said the central part of the storm first reached the coastline at 7:30 P. M. He estimated the top wind velocity at 60 miles an hour. At 8:15 P. M. he said the center of the disturbance would move into the Gulf of Mexico conside

| London.--(AP)--King Edward has chartered the yacht Nahlin for a three or four-week cruise along the Dalmatian coast, it was announced today at Buckingham Palace. The king will probably join the yacht in about ten days at Dubrovnik, Jugoslavia. He will be accompanied by three or four friends.

Orleans, Mass, July 28, (P)— Mark Harvey Liddell, 70, professor-emeritus of Purdue University and internationally known as an authority on Shakespeare, died at his Cape Cod home here early today. Liddell had lived here since his retirement seven years ago as professor of English and English Literature at Purdue. Early last spring he suffered a cerebral hemorrhage and has been ill since then. The noted educator and author was born at Clearfield, Pa., April 1, 1866, son of Thomas and Sophronia (Swan) Liddell. He took his bachelor’s degree from Princeton University in 1889 and did graduate work at both Oxford University in England and at the University of Berlin.

London, July 29.—(AP)—Six persons representing newspapers and newsreels were fined a total of 2,050 pounds (about $10,250) today for publishing captions on July 16 with the words ‘An attempt on the king's life' or ‘the King's assassination attempt.’ That was the day that George Andrew McMahon, a spectator at King Edward's military parade on Constitution Hill, drew a revolver as the monarch passed by on his horse. He says he did not intend to harm the king, but threw the weapon into the street as a “protest” against police “persecution.” The defendants were charged with contempt of court for prejudicing the case against McMahon before he was committed to trial accused of producing a weapon with “intent to alarm his majesty.”
LONDON, July 29.—Sir Samuel Hoare, first Lord of the Admiralty, announced today in the House of Commons the keels of two new British battleships would be laid in January of 1937.

PENSACOLA, Fla., July 28.—The coast guard late today ordered two cutters to investigate reports that missing British motorship Nunoca was damaged and in the Gulf of Mexico west of the Yucatan peninsula. A radio message from the commander of the New Orleans coast guard division said the captain of the port of Vera Cruz, Mexico, had received reports "that the English ship Nunoca probably is damaged near Isla Honda of Campeche." The coast guard was requested to send the information to all ships in the area and to relay it to the United States shipping board. The cutters Yeaton and Vigilant, both of which have been taking part in a widespread search for the Nunoca, were sent to the area. The 110-foot Nunoca left Grand Cayman Island for Tampa July 4 and has not been reported since. Thirteen passengers and a crew of nine were aboard.

(BY Associated Press) Brattleboro, Vt., July 29—Beatty S. Balestier, 69, of Dummerston, brother-in-law of the late Rudyard Kipling, died in the Memorial hospital here today. He had been ill since last December. His sister, Mrs. Kipling, is in England. His wife, May W. Mendon of New York, died in 1909. In 1923 he married Helen B. Banning of Walpole, N.H., who survives him.

1936-06-10.text: SHANGHAI —(4)— British authorities ordered women missionaries Wednesday from the Hengyang area of Hunan province, said to have been ‘occupied by advancing troops of the Canton (South China) government. Hunan lies immediately north of Kwangsi and Kwangtung provinces, which make up the Canton government, and is affiliated with the Nanking National government. Canton apparently is seeking to force Nanking into a joint war against Japan. General Ho Chien, governor of Hunan province, announced at Changsha the Canton forces occupied Hengyang. Hengyang is about 110 miles north of the Kwangtung border, halfway to Changsha, the capital.

BOSTON—Fear of story-book Indian scalpers and notorious gangsters made an English miss tremble as she landed here for an extensive tour of the United States. “Do you think I'll get scalped?” attractive Miss Kathleen Turner asked while walking down the gangplank. “And I do hope I'll not get into any trouble with gangsters.”

BALTIMORE, Md., June 10.—Dr. Francis E. Townsend prepared today to swing his old-age pension and share-the-wealth forces actively into every phase of the coming political campaign—except the presidential contest. He will leave late today for a speaking tour in New England after which he will go to Chicago for a meeting of the board of directors of his organization on June 15. The elderly leader of the Townsend $200-a-month pension movement said he “saw no choice” between President Roosevelt and Governor Alf. M. Landon, the probable Republican nominee. “They don't like us. We don’t like them,” Townsend said. “We shan't support either of them. We'll just concentrate on electing congressmen who favor our cause.”

WASHINGTON —()— Italy joined Great Britain Tuesday in defaulting anew on its semi-annual war debt payment to the United States, raising to $63,494,977 the amount of the Italian arrears. In the same routine fashion followed by the British government, Augusto Rosso, the Italian ambassador, notified Secretary Hull that his government regretted its inability at this time to offer any new proposals looking toward a settlement of the debt. His communication was in reply to the regular note dispatched by the State Department on May 22 reminding the Italian envoy that his country owed a new installment of $15,641,593 due next Monday. Including the regular semi-annual payment and installments already in arrears, a total of $1,160,122,766 will be due the United States from 13 countries on June 15.

HURLINGHAM CLUB, London, June 10.—America opened defense of the International Polo Cup today with a 10 to 9 victory over England before a fashionable crowd of 10,000. Eric Pedley, California star No. 1 on the American team, scored nine of the ten goals. This equalled Pedley's own record for cup competition, made in the second match of the 1930 series at Meadow Brook. ace, was the high spot of the challengers’ play.

Galesburg, IN, June 10.—(— Carter Davidson, professor of English at Carleton College, Northfield, Minn., today was named president of Knox College, succeeding Dr. Albert Britt, who resigned effective with the close of the June term. Dr. Davidson, who has been acting as assistant to the Carleton president, was graduated from Harvard in 1925. He received his master’s degree at the University of Louisville and completed work on his doctor's degree at the University of Chicago in 1930. He is an ordained Congregational minister. Born in Louisville, he is married and the father of one son. Trustees said he would take office about July.

FAIRBANKS, Alaska, June 10—(*)—Fire and water menaced sections of southeastern Alaska and northern British Columbia today while weather forecasts offered no relief from an unseasonable heat wave. Forest fires broke out in the hills above inundated valleys as high temperatures dried out timberlands and speeded the run-off of water from glaciers and snowfields. The Richardson highway near here was made impassable by washed out bridges and fills. The Yukon territory towns of Mayo and Dawson were cut off from the outside except by airplane and boat. Fresh food supplies were being rushed to both towns by plane.

VANCOUVER, B.C., June 9 — Glacier-fed rivers, swollen by an early thaw, sent new flood crests rolling down the Yukon and British Columbia Coasts tonight while a belated cold wave moved eastward to threaten wheat crops of the prairie provinces. The Columbia River, running bank full, swept into Washington state and virtually isolated Prescott, a small town near Rainier, Ore.

Great Britain and Italy are the guarantors of the Locarno treaty under which Germany, France and Belgium promised not to attack each other. When Reichsfuehrer Hitler moved troops into the demilitarized Rhineland, France alleged that he had broken the Locarno pact and the League of Nations council agreed with this interpretation. France called upon Great Britain and Italy to force Germany to withdraw those troops. Crisis in Africa But new Italian forces have conquered Ethiopian territory near Lake Tana, the source of the Nile, and consequently of major importance to Great Britain. Acting with speed, the British let it be known they regard the proposals as conciliatory, valuable and worthy of negotiation, despite the fact that Hitler has shown no penitence for his march into the Rhineland nor has contributed much to calm fears resulting from that action. Officials here, however, appeared to be dubious that the French and Belgians would as quickly see merit in Germany's suggestions. Hitler's program was handed to Foreign Secretary Anthony Eden today by Joachim von Ribbentrop, special German ambassador, along with an almost complete rejection of the proposals France, Britain, Belgium and Italy put forward a fortnight ago. A lengthy document outlining what Der Fuehrer is willing to do was submitted to the British government in London. Hitler promised—if his conditions are met—to sign 25-year peace pacts with France and Belgium and to return to the League of Nations. But within a few hours official French circles said Hitler's proposals are “unacceptable.” France, it was indicated, will insist upon an exchange of mutual assistance agreements among the four remaining Locarno powers. Great Britain appeared willing to accept many of Hitler’s proposals, which they regarded on the whole as conciliatory and worthwhile. Trenton, N. J.—(U.P)—One of the many reports filtering out of the Mercer county grand jury room today was that the jury wishes to postpone action on the Paul Wendel confession until Charles A. Lindbergh returns from England. The famous flier, it was reported, would be asked to tell the grand jury that he positively identified the body found after the kidnapping as that of his son. Lindbergh so testified at the trial of Bruno Richard Hauptmann.

No official source was willing to say whether the British had yet made any representations on the subject to Rome. However, an authoritative quarter reaffirmed the fact that Premier Mussolini had voluntarily, upon several occasions, given categorical assurance that Italy has no intentions of violating British interests in the Lake Tana region. It was believed possible that the British, who are showing increasing signs of irritation toward Italy because of the airplane bombings of Ethiopian civil centers and the reported use of poison gas, may instruct Sir Eric Drummond, the British ambassador to Rome, to call Mussolini’s attention to these Italian commitments at Lake Tana. LONDON, April 1 (A) — The British Air Ministry authorized Col. Charles A. Lindbergh today to fly his private plane over Great Britain — provided he does not engage in commercial flights or accept pay for his services. The American flier opened negotiations for the British approval two days ago when he appeared personally before American officials in London. “My name is Lindbergh,” he said then. “I want to renew my license. I am sorry to trouble you and hope it will not cause any difficulty.”

BEDFORD, April 2.—AP--Special prosecutor James R. Locke wound up his blistering cross-examination of Floyd Horton today by wringing from the farmer accused of the poison murder of his wife the admission she had refused to give him a divorce. The defense allowed Horton to step down from the stand finished and shaken without further questioning. Horton's fate, it appeared, soon will be in the jury's hands. Prosecutor Locke's rebuttal defense will be brief, he said. Defense Attorney Lucas reported five more witnesses will be called, but "it won't take much time for them." BEDFORD, April 2--AP—Attorneys saw a possibility today that the Horton poison murder trial might reach the jury next week. The defense which previously announced it would call "about 21 witnesses" already has presented nine with the defendant Floyd Horton still on the stand for cross-examination.

(By International News Service) ROME, April 2.--Premier Mussolini through his official press today warned England that League of Nations sanctions must be removed from Italy and the British fleet removed from the Mediterranean if headwaters of the Nile are to be respected. This warning followed announcement of the capture of Gondar, near Lake Tana in Ethiopia and amid reports that an Italian advance patrol has reached the shore of Lake Tana which feeds the Nile. The Italian foreign office denied any peace negotiations were in progress anywhere to end the Italo-Ethiopian war.

1936-05-19.text: London, May 19 (#) Italy may be invited to make changes in the staff of its London embassy, informed sources said today, in the Italo-Ethiopian-British dumdum bullet scandal. Certain members of parliament were understood to intend to question Anthony Eden concerning the position of the Italian military attache after the foreign secretary told the House of Commons yesterday an attempt had been made to “fabricate evidence” that British interests supplied illegal ammunition to Ethiopia. The government was being pressed, informed sources said, to take up the entire question of the embassy’s association with a “Colonel Pedro Lopez” whom Eden described as a “notorious purveyor of false information and forged documents.” Eden declared “Lopez”, a British subject of Polish origin, posed as an Ethiopian agent, obtained ammunition samples from a British firm through forged letters and used the samp

WASHINGTON, May 19—The United States prepared today to adhere to the new tri-power naval treaty, speedily ratified by the Senate after it was variously dubbed “futile,” “disappointing,” and the best “under existing world conditions.” The pact signed by the United States, Great Britain and France, which becomes effective January 1, was ratified yesterday without a record vote after two hours of debate. The treaty limits the sizes of the signatories’ guns and warcraft and provides for an exchange of information in naval construction programs. (Abandonment of any of the treaty’s provisions is permitted in case of war or in the event that non-signatory powers engage in excessive building activities.) ()—The assertion that a “notorious purveyor of false information and forged documents” gave Italy “fabricated evidence” that Ethiopia bought dumdum bullets in England was made today before the House of Commons by Foreign Secretary Anthony Eden. The British Foreign Office, Eden said, warned the Italian government that a self-styled “Colonel Pedro Lopez,” said to have been Italy's informant, was unreliable. The Foreign Secretary made clear that despite this “friendly warning” to Dino Grandi, the Italian Ambassador, Lopez’ relations with the Italian embassy continued. Italian allegations that Ethiopians used dumdum bullets supplied from England were based on “what could only be described as a fabrication of evidence,” the Foreign Secretary asserted. | By Associated Press LONDON. May 19. - The British government says that the lesser naval powers have started construction of over 200 submarines since 1930. This statement, disclosed today, was made in Britain's note to Washington from Tokyo May 8. In the note, the British invoked an escape clause, permitting naval increase under certain conditions, of the 1930 London naval treaty. The lesser powers represent the navy owning nations exclusive of Great Britain, the United States, and Japan.

London—(/)—Chester Davis, AAA administrator, returned to London today in a somewhat gloomy and pessimistic mood after six weeks of an agricultural survey in 11 European countries. He will sail for home Thursday aboard the S. S. Washington. While Davis feels farmers in the United States can gradually expand their sales to Europe, he nevertheless expressed the view the United States can never recapture its former markets for big and important commodities, because of the increase of self-sufficiency programs and the erection of stern trade barriers.

ROME, May 19—(AP)—Italian press reports today said 498 political exiles have been returned to their homes from Italian islands in a prelude to what is expected to be an “unprecedented” amnesty declaration of May 24.

Babs Rati la are ear ra eo area ae sc NAPLES, May 19-(#)—The Italian hospital ship California arrived from East Africa today, bearing 1321 sick and wounded. The steamship Aquilea also arrived, bringing under-secretary of State for Colonies Alessandro Lessona.

ST. IVES, CORNWALL, ENG., May 19 — Marmaduke William Pickthall, 61, a successful novelist for more than 30 years, died today. Among Pickthall’s better known novels are “Pot-Au-Feu,” “With the Turk in War Time,” and “The Meaning of the Glorious Koran.”

1936-01-27.text: . Copyright 1986 By United Press LONDON, Jan. 27 UP. Thousands upon thousands of people rich and poor, young and old poured into Central London today, hoping to view King George's coffin as it lay for the last day in Westminster Hall. From all over great, sprawling London and from every part of the British Isles people converged upon the Westminster area. Whatever the weather tomorrow, Edward VIII and his brothers, the Dukes of York, Gloucester and Kent, will walk behind the coffin on the 3 1/2 mile funeral route to Paddington railway station, where the late king's body will leave for Windsor for burial in the Royal Chapel, St. George's. Tonight Edward entertains heads of foreign delegations at dinner at Buckingham Palace in accordance with precedent.

London, Jan. 26 (#)—Churches throughout the empire revered the late King George V at memorial services today while foreign royal and governmental delegations to Tuesday's State funeral poured into London. The Archbishop of Canterbury, conducting the principal service at Westminster Abbey, pointed to the late ruler’s home life in the course of an eloquent tribute, and urged the nation to make marriage a more stable institution. “While marriage is becoming to be regarded with so much recklessness and frivolity,” he said, “remember the home life of King George and keep your homes pure and stable.” The Queen Mother, with the Duke and Duchess of Gloucester; the Duke and Duchess of Kent; the Princess Royal, her husband, the Earl of Harewood and their two sons attended a service in the private chapel of Buckingham Palace. Reports reaching Rome and Italy's southern “hell on wheels” column rumbled onward past Neghelli, aiming seemingly at Allato, major city of Sidamo Province, hundreds of miles from its starting point. Heavy hostilities apparently continued on the northern Ethiopian front, with conflicting Italian and Ethiopian claims of victory still unreconciled. And in Rome, Il Duce's government listened anxiously for details from contracting sanctionist powers on their new “Mediterranean understanding.” Rome's Anger Grows Great Britain, France and the League of Nations awaited developments in the sanctions situation. LONDON, Jan. 27.—King Edward VIII designated the widowed Queen Mary, his mother, as “The Queen Mother” today, thereby ending a controversy as to her proper title. By his special command, the prayers in the order of service for all churches in England during the late King George's funeral Tuesday, read in part: “We commend, O Lord, to Thy Fatherly goodness; Mary, the Queen Mother, and all members of the Royal family.”

1 BAUINESUIIN, Va. eee 1 Oe (Sunday Express says the historic and rich duchy of Cornwall will be turned over by King Edward to the Duke of York to aid the latter financially in his increased duties as heir-apparent. This move was viewed in some quarters as the strongest indication the bachelor king never intends to marry, the paper said, for Cornwall, since it was established by Edward III, always has been the property of the heir to the throne. It was suggested that if Edward had any intention of marrying he probably would keep the duchy for a possible son and heir, in accordance with age-old tradition. (The income from the duchy of Cornwall was the sole state revenue for the Prince of Wales. In 1927 it paid him £72,817—about $365,000.)

| LONDON, Jan. 37.—King Carol of Roumania has shocked royal circles again by his open devotion to Mme. Magda Lupescu, the sweetheart for whose love he once renounced his right to the throne. Carol took Mme. Lupescu with him when he left for London to attend the funeral of King George, his cousin. She stayed in Paris, awaiting him there. Dowager Queen Marie of Roumania refused to accompany her son on his royal train, and it is now announced that a cold will make it impossible for her to attend the funeral. King George was her first cousin.

By United Press, CAIRO, Jan. 27.—Many casualties were reported today when police fired on student strikers rioting at Mansura and Damanhur. The students struck, as have most students here, in protest against British domination. Students here considerably damaged the Arts and Crafts School and fired on streetcars. Soldiers had to reinforce police.

DOGRN, The Netherlands, Jan. 27 (P)—White-bearded Wilhelm of Hohenzollern, former kaiser of Germany, became 77 years old today, still proudly erect and enjoying firm health. Formal observance of his birthday anniversary was postponed until Friday in respect to the memory of his cousin, King George of England, who will be buried tomorrow at Windsor. Even the exercises arranged for Friday were restricted to the family and immediate household.

1936-09-27.text: (Copyright, 1936, by Associated Press) PARIS, Sept. 26.—(#)—Financially harassed France, allied with Great Britain and the United States in a “monetary equilibrium” program, looked ahead today to a formal embargo on gold exports preliminary to proposed devaluation of the franc. Members of Premier Leon Blum’s cabinet and the governing board of the Bank of France labored to prepare measures for submission to a special session of Parliament Monday. The proposed statutes, an official announcement declared, would reduce “approximately one third” the franc’s gold content. The Bourse—stock market was closed “for several days” as details of the suggested monetary revision were worked out. Informed quarters expected the gold embargo, which must bear approval of the governor of the Bank of France, would be proclaimed formally today to halt the flow of gold from the country. PARIS, Sept. 26. (UP)—The French government decided today to devalue the franc—possibly by one-fourth or one-third of its current value—through an agreement with the United States and Great Britain that may bring world-wide currency adjustment. Parliament meets in extraordinary session Monday to legalize the devaluation and give the government power to requisition all gold at the current rate. The Bank of France already has ceased gold deliveries to individuals so that technically France—mainstay of the gold bloc nations—is off the gold standard. The United States and Great Britain have assured France the "use of all means to prevent monetary difficulties." That is interpreted to mean the giant stabilization funds of the two nations will be used to prevent raids on the new franc. Other nations were urged to cooperate. With the French parliament summoned for an extraordinary session Monday and steps taken to halt the drain of gold from Paris, the franc was regarded in financial quarters as on the verge of joining the circle of currency devaluation traceable to the outbreak of the European money crisis more than five years ago. The historic tri-partite accord, announced simultaneously in three of the world’s greatest money capitals, came as a dramatic climax to weeks of delicate negotiations leading to abandonment of the gold standard by France. The pact rests solely upon the good faith of the three nations. Under it the United States and England agree to devaluation of the French franc and promise to refrain from any retaliatory measures such as further devaluation of the pound and the dollar. The agreement is designed to: 1. Pave the way for permanent and effective stabilization of world currencies. 2. WASHINGTON, Sept. 26.—The United States government threw five million dollars of its stabilization fund into the exchange market today to halt what Secretary Morgenthau described as a Russian attempt to drive down the pound sterling. This action followed the new French, British and American agreement to prevent a disturbance of the international exchange.

The question was revived here just a day after Leon Blum, France’s socialist leader and premier-to-be, announced he would like to see the debt “misunderstanding” erased, with Paris indicating the first move was more likely to come from London. In the background of renewed consideration of the problem left by the World War, informed sources said, rested the possibility of gaining American assistance in any general economic reorganization to help avert the danger of a new war. LONDON, (UP).—Ethiopia has completed the establishment of a secret government to keep alive its identity and refute the Italian claim to its conquest, Emperor Haile Selassie telephoned from Jerusalem today to his minister to Great Britain, Ajaz Martin. Before he left Addis Ababa, fleeing from the advancing Italians, the Emperor told Martin, several of his ministers and generals left for the west to set up a government. He mandated the leaders to rule for him in his absence. Seat of the government, it was learned, is at Gore, in the Ilu Babor district of Gomma province, 225 miles west of Addis Ababa and 105 miles from the Sudan frontier, in a region never approached by the Italians. British official reports are that the government is actually functioning. It is believed that the government is headed by Ras Desta Demtu, Haile Selassie’s son-in-law.

FRANKFORT ON THE MAIN, Germany, May 17.—(Sunday)—()—The Zeppelin Hindenburg, held here for hours by ill winds, took off at 5:35 a.m. today (11:35 p.m., E.S.T., Saturday) on its second flight to Lakehurst, N.J.

Frankfort on the Main, Germany — Dr. Hugo Eckener, veteran zeppelin commander, decided Saturday to remain in Germany and not to accompany the Hindenburg Saturday night on its second regular trans-Atlantic flight to the United States. His decision had no connection with his controversy with the Nazi propaganda ministry. Forty passengers registered for the second voyage to Lakehurst, and the Hindenburg, pronounced in perfect condition, took on its fuel and freight. The great airliner was to leave its base again at 8:00 p.m. (1:00 p.m. C.S.T.) Saturday night for America. Capt. Ernst Lehmann, commander of the sky cruiser, who watched mechanics oil the machines, said an examination showed the motors were working perfectly and there was not so much as a single screw to be tightened. ROME, May 16 (4.--The Italian senate ratified today the decrees annexing Ethiopia and creating the new Roman empire. The bill was presented by Gug-Nemo Marconi, the inventor, to the presence of Premier Mussolini and ministers of the Italian cabinet. Marconi urged passage of the measure in a strong address and was followed by the fascist dictator who requested the legislative body to give the proposal urgent consideration.

DY LN ASSOCIATION Fives, ADDIS ABABA, May 16.—Native runners returning from Southern Ethiopia reported tonight all the American and foreign missionaries were safe. Authorities sent out the sure-footed Africans along the crude trails to determine how some three-score Americans and other foreigners had survived the war. The Americans, all missionaries and their families stationed in such remote villages as Gofa, Kambata, Jimma and Wolamo, have been out of communication with the capital since Mussolini's armies seized Addis Ababa. Authorities here, noting signs of increasing hostility by natives against all whites, felt uneasy about the scattered Americans. They said however, they had no definite reason to believe any had been harmed. The runners will seek to reach the Americans and bring back news of their condition. An American military observer, Major Norman E. Fiske, reached Addis Ababa

1936-04-18.text: London, April 17—()—Great Britain raised the strength of its grand fleet in the Mediterranean to a new peak today, while British opinion, stung by renewed attacks of the Italian press, appeared to harden against Fascist Italy. Fifteen new mine-sweepers were dispatched to Gibraltar, at the eastern entrance of the Mediterranean, to join the anti-submarine flotillas already there. Naval observers estimated that 190 British warships were on in or near the Mediterranean—the greatest number since the start of the Italo-Ethiopian conflict last October. British sources foresaw stronger support for a stern policy at Geneva in the conciliation committee of 13's negotiations to bring peace between Italy and Ethiopia. Italy’s demands for direct negotiations, termed here a “conqueror’s peace,” aroused bitter opposition in some British quarters and brought forth demands for “vigorous and devastating”

(Copyright, 1936, By The Associated Press) London, April 18--The British government, already harassed by the delicate Ethiopian and Rhineland situations, looked for clarification today of reports that Turkey had remilitarized the Dardanelles in violation of post-war treaties. Dispatches from Istanbul, former capital of Turkey on the Bosporus, across the Sea of Marmora from the Dardanelles, said troops moved into the demilitarized zone yesterday on the straits between the Marmora and Aegean Seas. The soldiers moved in without any public announcement, the dispatches said, after a meeting of the Turkish cabinet presided over by President Kemal Ataturk. A Reuters (British) news agency dispatch from Ankara, present capital of Turkey, however, said the semi-official news agency there denied that Turkish troops occupied the zone. The bilateral agreement, described as an armistice, resulted from talks between Anthony Eden, British foreign secretary, and Joseph Paul-Boncour, French minister of state. Settlement of the divergent opinions, French sources asserted, was arrived at as the league conciliation committee assembled to review its own failure to bring peace to East Africa and after the league council was called for a special session Monday. France, desirous of Italian support in the Rhineland controversy, has been favorable toward lifting of existing sanctions

LONDON, April 18.—-(UP)—Turkey’s promise that it would support Great Britain in event of an attack by Italy was expected today to make certain there would be no real opposition to its reoccupation of the Dardanelles in emulation of Germany's remilitarisation of the Rhineland. Officials were understood to have been astonished at news that Turkish soldiers had occupied the straits. The Turkish note of April 11, notifying Lausanne treaty powers of the country's intention of reclaiming full sovereignty over the straits—including their defense—clearly indicated readiness to negotiate before acting. Increasing tension in the Mediterranean was believed the factor which caused the change in President Mustapha Kemal Ataturk's plans to seek consent of the treaty signatories.

PARIS—(AP)—United States authorities in Paris announced today they were informed that British police found a woman, sought in connection with a New York bond theft case, last night in a London hotel. The woman's husband, also wanted for questioning about the activities of an alleged bond theft ring which dealt in millions of dollars, was still missing, the authorities said, while the search spread across all of Europe. Officials said two suspects arrested here would be held in jail until a New York detective, sailing from New York today, arrived. Extradition proceedings were delayed by lack of evidence connecting the suspects with the New York bond robberies.

Oxford, England, April 17— Death is a pleasant, musical affair—at least when temporary—according to Miss Daisy Allan, a 22-year-old brunette, who lives to tell of her experience today although her heart was stilled for 15 minutes. A new drug injected by Dr. Justin Bailey, supplemented by artificial respiration, brought Daisy “back to life.” “I heard faint music,” the feminine Lazarus said. “Everything was very peaceful. It was like nothing I have ever known before. “I seemed to be suspended all the time, with soft music playing. There was no pain, no terror—only peace and rest.

. Paris, France —(A.P.)— A plan to fortify Belgium against any German attack was reported by the newspaper as the outcome of the discussions. The paper said it “understands” that the British asked Belgium to create a defensive line from Antwerp to Ghent, on Belgium's northern frontier, with construction of two forts and provision for flooding the line to block any invasion. British air officers were understood to have insisted that in case of an alarm, they could immediately use Belgian aviation fields, either civil or military. The Intransigeant reported that new Belgian air fields would be prepared rapidly. Belgium also would study the possibility of completing speedily a line of defense which would extend from France’s Maginot line of fortifications on the east, the newspaper said. The Albert canal, toward the north, this report said, would be connected with the southeast area.

Two thousand English men and women paraded around Winson Green prison Wednesday, protesting while British justice hanged Dory Waddingham, thirty-four years old mother of five children, one of whom was only six months old. She had committed murder; and in England when you commit murder they hang you, protest or no protest. The crowd, led by Mrs. Violet Van Der Elst, who objects to any capital punishment, was orderly. Some knelt and prayed. Only the new King Edward could have saved the woman's life and English kings are too wise to meddle with law. The woman had murdered with poison a patient in her nursing home and the patient’s daughter to get an $8,000 legacy, willed to her by the victim. The trap was sprung, a black flag was run up on the prison flagstaff, women kneeled, praying and weeping, and had hanged the ninth woman in this century. They HANG them in England and they have few mur

1936-02-12.text: At least 65 persons were known to have been killed and many injured by storms which harassed most of Europe today from the British Isles to the Aegean. The storm in England had taken a toll of 21. Sixteen were dead in Italy and 15 in northern Greece. Thirteen were killed and eight injured in a Bulgarian train wreck caused by a blizzard. Earthquakes added to the troubles of dwellers in Macedonia. Several vessels in the Aegean sent out distress calls.

{ASSOCIATED PRESS} BERLIN, Feb. 12 — (AP) — Charges of collusion between Roman Catholics and Communists were heard in Germany today as at least 100 Catholics and Communists were under arrest after simultaneous raids by secret police. Catholics were particularly charged with conspiracy with Communists in the Rhineland, the scene of the police round-up. The official organ of Adolf Hitler’s black-shirt guards, Das Schwarze Korps, issued a sharp challenge today to charges that the Catholic church in Germany was being persecuted. The fact that the “Catholic church feels itself menaced and persecuted in national socialist Germany” can be clearly seen in sermons and pastoral letters, the publication said. In reality, the organ asserted, it was the old story, as “old as the church itself,” which Das Schwarze Korps said, always raises a cry of “persecution” whenever its political ambitions were t

TOKYO, Feb. 12 (4)—A detach- ment of Japanese and Manchukuoan soldiers was reported today to have defeated a group of 100 Mongolians in a battle of several hours at Olahudka, southwest of Lake Bor. The battle, as reported by the Hsinking correspondent of the Domei News Agency, was on the largest scale of any of the clashes which have occurred recently between the Soviet-advised Mongolians and the Japanese-controlled Manchukuans. The report did not give details of the battle, other than to say the Mongolians were compelled to evacuate Olahudka. There was no indication as to what casualties there may have been. Olahudka is in disputed territory. The Mongols claim it is in Outer Mongolia while the Japanese claim it is in Manchukuo.

ADDIS ABABA, Feb. 11 (#)—A shackled American missionary and his Canadian colleague, held prisoners in the southwestern war zone by a local Ethiopian chieftain, have been ordered released, it was disclosed today. The men are the Rev. Harold Street of Paxton, Ill., who was imprisoned with a dog chain fastened to his legs, and the Rev. John Trewin of Toronto, who was not shackled. Mrs. Street and her four children were held under guard at a mission station. Crown Prince Asfa Wosan of Ethiopia, it was learned, ordered release of the North Americans two days ago, but because of a lack of communication facilities with southwestern Gamo province it could not be learned immediately if the order was carried out. The missionaries, attached to the Sudan Interior Mission, had refused to leave the danger zone when ordered to do so by Ethiopian provincial officials. A letter received by the government

Berlin. Feb. 12 (UP)—The government issued an ordinance today marshalling for labor and military service all German citizens living temporarily or permanently abroad. The ordinance published in the Official Gazette was signed by the Ministers of Interior, War and Foreign Affairs. It provides that every German citizen abroad, including those carrying double citizenship, must report to the German consulate as soon as his class is called up. He must obey the consul's orders for medical examination, the date for which will be fixed by the consul. Those whom the consul finds fit, both physically and as to 'Aryan descent' must ordinarily pay their own traveling and other expenses to and from Germany.

The fact that the "Catholic church feels itself menaced and persecuted in national socialist Germany" can be clearly seen in sermons and pastoral letters, the publication said. Wholesale Arrests In reality, the organ asserted, it was the old story, as "old as the church itself," which Das Schwarze Korps said, always raises a cry of "persecution" whenever its political ambitions were thwarted. The "SS" organ took its stand while Nazi secret police roamed the Catholic Rhineland district, making what informed sources said appeared to be the greatest number of wholesale arrests since scores of nuns and monks were seized a year ago. Reports of the arrests spread rapidly, by word of mouth, with anxiety increased by see

Berlin, Feb. 12, (UP)—Adolf Hitler angrily denounced Jewry as a “sinister power” today in delivering the funeral oration at Schwerin for Wilhelm Gustloff, leader of German Nazis in Switzerland, who was assassinated at Davos by David Frankfurter, 26, Jewish medical student from Jugoslavia. Hitler charged Jews with responsibility for Germany’s troubles of the last decade, as well as for political terror. He referred to “the Jewish enemy” as he raised his voice and said: “But we shall take up the gauntlet.” Addressing the coffin, Hitler continued: “you did not die in vain.”

BERLIN, Feb. 12.— (AP) — Germany’s secret police took control today of the subordinate civil administration under a new law published in the official gazette. District governors were ordered to take commands from secret police headquarters after a series of raids resulting from charges of collusion between Roman Catholics and Communists. The secret police arrested more than 100 Catholics and Communists who allegedly conspired together against the government. The police round-up centered in the Rhineland. District governors, after receiving orders from the secret police, will pass on the instructions to local police headquarters with such directions as may be desirable. The official organ of Adolf Hitler's black-shirt guards, Das Schwarze Korps, issued a sharp challenge to charges that the Catholic church in Germany was being persecuted. 1936-11-30.text: ABOARD the U.S.S. Chester at sea, Nov. 19 (President Roosevelt sailed southward today aboard the cruiser Indianapolis en route to the epoch-making inter-American peace conference at Buenos Aires in December. Flying the president's flag, the ship continued to average about nine knots as they neared the tropics. The president will stop for a day at Rio De Janeiro November 27, where he will be honored by Brazil. He may address a joint session of the Brazilian parliament.

LONDON, Nov. 30 (UP)--Sources usually acquainted with the cabinet's activities said today Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin has informed King Edward he can expect no support from government or parliament for a possible marriage to Mrs. Wallis Simpson. This was reliably understood to be the result of two dramatic secret meetings which Baldwin had shortly after a surprise cabinet meeting. The first meeting was with Clement Attlee, labor party leader, the second with the king. The government viewed the situation as so delicate that all reference to Baldwin's visit to the king was omitted from the court circular, which customarily records such visits automatically. It was understood Baldwin's meeting with Atlee established a common front of conservative and labor.

| London, Nov. 30--Foreign Minister Anthony Eden dampened French hopes of a tri-power military accord between Great Britain, France and Belgium today. “His Majesty’s Government,” the youthful foreign minister told the House of Commons, “has explicitly deprecated any tendency to divide the world into conflicting camps. “Our policy continues to be to promote friendly relations between all nations,” (Reports from Paris today said that Foreign Minister Yvon Delbos would announce an agreement Friday that was virtually a tripartite military accord between Britain, France and Belgium.)

|. GATRO, Egypt, Nov. 30, (AP)--Capt, James A. Mollison and Capt, Ed- guard Corniglion-Molinier sped away from here today after a brief refueling stop on their attempted speed flight from England to South Africa. Mollison and Corniglion-Molinier, his co-pilot, took off yesterday from Croydon, England, in the “Dorothy,” speed plane in which Mollison broke the west-east Atlantic crossing time last Oct. 30. They aimed to set a new record for the flight from Croydon, Eng. to Capetown, South Africa, and return. The existing marks, both ways, are held by Mollison’s wife, Amy, who flew to South Africa in three days, six hours, 26 minutes, and returned in four days, 16 hours and 18 minutes.

PARIS. NOV. 3.—Announcement of a virtual three-power military accord among France, Great Britain and Belgium will be announced by Foreign Minister Yvon Delbos Friday, informed sources said today. Delbos will return last week’s assurance from British Foreign Secretary Anthony Eden that the two nations will come to each other's assistance if attacked by another nation, it was said. Both France and Great Britain will extend similar guarantees to Belgium, authoritative sources reported. The projected accord was interpreted in some quarters as signaling a new Western European pact. Eden Speaks The British declaration was made last Friday when Foreign Secretary Anthony Eden spoke at a luncheon in honor of Premier Paul Van Zeeland of Belgium. “Let us once again affirm that the independence and integrity of Belgium is of vital interest to this nation and that Belgium can count on our help were s

By The Associated Press Cairo, Egypt—Captain James A. Mollison and Captain Edouard Corniglion-Molinier arrived here today on their projected speed dash from Croydon, England, to Capetown, South Africa. It was a scheduled refueling stop.

Cairo, Egypt—(U.P)—James A. Mollison, seeking a new London-Capetown flight record, arrived here at 3:30 A.M. Monday and continued his flight at 5:25 A.M. after refueling. He is accompanied by Edouard Colignion of France as co-pilot.

1936-06-18.text: 'LONDON (AP) - Italy has con- quered Ethiopia and Great Britain does not intend to go to war in the Mediterranean to change the situation, Foreign Secretary Anthony Eden told the House of Commons Thursday in a general debate on foreign affairs. Great Britain favors lifting of League of Nations sanctions against Italy and an effort to come to terms in Europe. The government is not prepared to take military action,” Eden said. Earlier Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin assured the House that Great Britain's rearmament is being speeded up because of the dangerous situation in Europe.

NASSAU, The Bahamas, June 17 — Colonial authorities received unconfirmed reports today that shipwreck and death on the pink sands of a tropical coral cay may have overtaken a crew of British fishermen who turned their prosaic trawler into a treasure hunting argosy. A wrecked vessel, flying the British ensign and answering the description of the missing Girl Pat, was found on a tiny island in the Eastern Bahamas, the report said, along with three bodies. There also were personal effects, navigating instruments, and a Bible. The sloop Dove from Ackling Island made the find. Its crew buried the bodies and reported the discovery of a second sloop which relayed the word here. The scene of the shipwreck was Samana, also known as Atwood Cay, about 300 miles southeast of Nassau and just northwest of Silver Bank, where legend says 17 Spanish galleons loaded with treasure were sunk by pirates. London, June 18—(#)—George Bernard Shaw, informed of the death of the Russian author, Maxim Gorky, said today: “T dare say it’s time for all us nineteenth century writers to clear out, “You'd better prepare my obituary, “You never know.”

PARIS, June 18—(UP).—The American colony mobilized today to help tired doctors and nurses, swabbing floors and stoking furnaces in the American hospital, after the French foreign office refused a request of U. S. Ambassador Jesse Isidor Straus that the government force the evacuation of striking employees barricaded in the hospital laundry. The hospital board appealed to the American colony to help maintain hospital services and succor 25 patients seriously ill and 50 others who may have to be transferred to other institutions. The strike of 100 workers, 60 of whom are occupying parts of the hospital, forced the hospital to refuse new patients. Theodore Rousseau, president of the American club, appealed for volunteers at a luncheon, At once the American Legion, the women’s club, the junior guild, church groups and students met to draft plans and divide emergency hospital work, Refusing S

PARIS —(/)}— Street fighting between nationalists and leftists in Marseilles and violence in far-off Algeria darkened the French strike picture Wednesday night. Several were wounded at Marseilles. Mobile guards intervened when a group of 5,000 striking members of the leftist "Peoples’ Front" attacked a parade of 3,000 nationalists on the main street. Many fought with knives. Town Evacuated The center of town was completely evacuated by order of authorities. Police and mobile guards patrolled the streets. In Algeria, officials said agrarian workers in some sections plundered the countryside led by "foreign agitators." Their appeals for reinforcements from barracks in Algeria were granted. At home, the senate quickly voted bills giving workers paid vacations and relieving veterans who are job holders from a reduction in their pensions. Debate on a 40-hour week

MADRID, (4?) — Prison riots and a new walkout of 100,000 store employees in Barcelona sent Spain's labor fever mounting today. Civil guards were mobilized to put down disorders in Alcalá de Henares prison near the capital as looting and burning broke inside the walls. One Is Wounded One prisoner was wounded by the guards during the riots. Four guards suffered injuries in suppressing the noisy inmates who broke windows and furniture, and set fire to their beds and mattresses. Convicts began the disorders to protest against confinement of several of their companions in underground cells for infractions of prison rules. Demand Higher Wages Store and shop workers in Barcelona, the city and province, marched from their posts in support of demands for higher wages. A general strike tied up the entire city of Cadiz, the workers quitting in sympathy with striking.

BRUSSELS, June 18.—W.9—The government drafted decrees today authorizing the requisitioning of food as Belgium's strike of 200,000 workers spread alarmingly. Measures to provide emergency food transport were prepared. Although the strikes, now in their fourth day, spread through textile factories, there were few disorders. Demonstrators burned a canal bridge near Mons. Soldiers were summoned to rebuild it. Premier Paul Van Zeeland ordered emergency precautions while working for agreements to make it possible for strikers to return to their jobs before Monday.

Paris .(#)—French government officials resolved today to forcibly eject the strikers who have crippled operations at the American hospital if they refuse to come to terms. Reconsidering their first reply to a personal appeal from Jesse Isidor Straus, the American ambassador, officials said forceful action would be taken unless the strikers return to work under a contemplated compromise offer. CONFERENCE TONIGHT The effect the compromise, a meeting was arranged for tonight between delegates of the general federation of labor and the hospital.

1936-11-29.text: | ABOARD THE U.S.S. CHESTER At Sea — President Roosevelt, already at work on his second major speech in South America, sailed southward today for Buenos Aires and the inter-American peace conference. The cruiser Indianapolis pulled out of Rio De Janeiro’s harbor last night after a 12-hour visit in which hopes for strengthened relations between Brazil and the United States were reaffirmed on both sides. “I am leaving you tonight with great regret,” the chief executive of the United States told President Getulio Vargas of Brazil shortly before his cruiser departed. “One thing, however, I shall remember—that is that it was two people who invented the New Deal—the President of Brazil and the President of the United States.” Mr. Roosevelt said inter-continental airplane service had made international friendship more easy to achieve. He invited Brazilians to visit the United States, not only f
